comment: The Lifelong Health Record is presented as a component. In federated systems it is not a component but a governed view assembled on request from source systems that remain authoritative. Presenting it as a component invites the reading that a central longitudinal store is intended, which is precisely the reading that has defeated national programmes politically.

public.text: The Lifelong Health Record is presented as a component. In federated systems it is not a component but a governed view assembled on request from source systems that remain authoritative. Presenting it as a component invites the reading that a central longitudinal store is intended, which is precisely the reading that has defeated national programmes politically.
public.suggestedRevision: Describe the Lifelong Health Record at the two levels the draft already uses for registries: at governance level a single authoritative longitudinal view with defined provenance and attribution; at implementation level a store, a federated view, or a hybrid. State explicitly that a federated implementation satisfies the architecture. In the Netherlands this distinction is decisive: the 2011 Bill was rejected on the concern that data would be centralised, while the architecture in fact kept data at source.
